requirements.title: SEQUENTIAL= returns YES or NO for determinable allowed-access method membership
requirements.definition: SEQUENTIAL= is assigned YES if SEQUENTIAL is included in the set of allowed access methods for the file and NO if SEQUENTIAL is not included in that set.

pending.sequential-yes-token: Open a file with ACCESS="SEQUENTIAL", initialize SEQUENTIAL to sentinels, inquire, and assert only that SEQUENTIAL is in {YES, UNKNOWN}: 12.10.2.29 p1 assigns YES when SEQUENTIAL is included in the allowed access methods, but also assigns UNKNOWN if the processor is unable to determine that membership.
pending.sequential-no-token: No unconditional portable NO oracle: no source in this packet requires a processor-independent file to exclude SEQUENTIAL from its allowed access methods. A future test that first establishes exclusion by another portable rule may assert only membership in {NO, UNKNOWN}, because 12.10.2.29 p1 permits UNKNOWN when the processor is unable to determine membership.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive INQUIRE plans first establish the connection or file state being observed, initialize every inquiry variable to a nonmatching sentinel value, execute INQUIRE, and assert only values fixed by 12.10.2: exact tokens such as UNDEFINED or UNKNOWN, logical true/false where specified, zero/nonzero IOSTAT where 12.11 later permits it, or bounded set membership where the source gives a set. Processor-dependent file names, case interpretation, multi-unit choices, file storage unit counts, asynchronous completion policy, IOMSG text, and numeric status codes are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself is a numbered syntax rule or numbered constraint and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. Undefined inquiry variables are not read as an oracle; IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never compared.

requirements.title: SEQUENTIAL= returns UNKNOWN for an unconnected unit inquiry
requirements.definition: SEQUENTIAL= is assigned UNKNOWN if the unit identified by file-unit-number is not connected to a file.

pending.sequential-unconnected-unit-unknown-toke: Open and close a known external unit so it is not connected to a file, initialize SEQUENTIAL to sentinels, inquire by UNIT= for that unit, and expect UNKNOWN.

requirements.title: SEQUENTIAL= UNKNOWN for inability to determine allowed access methods is processor latitude
requirements.definition: SEQUENTIAL= is assigned UNKNOWN if the processor is unable to determine whether SEQUENTIAL is included in the set of allowed access methods for the file.

pending.sequential-unable-to-determine-unknown-l: No portable oracle can force processor inability to determine allowed access methods for a particular file; this latitude is recorded separately from the required unconnected-unit UNKNOWN result.

accounting.rationale: SEQUENTIAL= mixes required YES/NO and unconnected-unit UNKNOWN results with processor latitude for inability to determine the allowed access methods.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10, the INQUIRE statement and all thirty-four inquiry specifiers (batch165). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across three rounds. Round 1 split the 'unable to determine' latitude out of eight YES/NO/UNKNOWN specifiers and out of ENCODING and SIZE; round 2 made the plans assert only what that latitude leaves portable - membership in {YES, UNKNOWN} for a method in use, and {POS-1, -1} for the size of a stream file. R1230, R1231 and C1247-C1251 were pre-accounted. With this packet Clause 12 is fully registered. Source accounting only.
